fullDescription:
Bai Tu Long is the bay northeast of Ha Long proper, and it is the one almost nobody books.

The three bays are one continuous karst landscape divided by administration rather than geology. Ha Long carries the fleet, Lan Ha sits south off Cat Ba, and Bai Tu Long runs northeast towards the Chinese border. Licensing limits how many boats can work Bai Tu Long, so the routes there are genuinely quiet in a way Ha Long has not been for twenty years.

The legend that names them is worth knowing. Ha Long means descending dragon: a mother dragon sent down to defend Vietnam, who spat jade that became the islands. Bai Tu Long is where her children came down after her. The names are a pair, and locals use them that way.

The one-day and two-day options are different trips rather than different lengths. A day cruise stays in the busier central water. The two-day version reaches Bai Tu Long and includes the night, which is when the bay empties out entirely, plus a welcome drink and hot and cold towels on arrival.

If you have the night to spare, the overnight is the version worth booking here specifically, because the quiet water is the whole reason to pick Bai Tu Long over the famous bay.

We book with Tinny Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers bottled water, with hotel pickup and drop-off, the welcome drink and the towels depending on the option selected.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Bai Tu Long, northeast towards the Chinese border
Licensing caps the boats, so the water is genuinely quiet
Named for the dragon children, after Ha Long's mother dragon
One day stays central; two days reaches Bai Tu Long
The overnight is the version that justifies this route

fullDescription:
Both bays in a single day on a yacht, which is the only realistic way to reach Lan Ha without an overnight.

Lan Ha lies south of Ha Long proper, off Cat Ba Island: the same drowned karst, around 300 islands, and a fraction of the boats because the big fleet stays north. Standard day cruises cannot get there and back in the time, so a faster boat is what makes it possible.

Six hours on the water covering both bays means a full day rather than a gentle one, and the yacht is doing real distance. The upside is that you see the postcard bay and the quiet bay in the same trip instead of choosing.

A Vietnamese buffet lunch is served on board along with a welcome drink.

Round-trip shared car transfer from Hanoi is optional rather than included, which matters: Hanoi to Ha Long is around two and a half hours each way, so without it you need your own way to the pier and back. Check whether your option covers it before booking.

This is the trip for people with one day in northern Vietnam who would rather see more water than more cabins. If you have a night to spare, an overnight reaches the same places more slowly and with the bay to yourself after dark.

We book with Luxury Vietnam Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the luxury day cruise, a welcome drink on board and a Vietnamese buffet lunch, with the Hanoi car transfer if your option includes it.

Six hours. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Reaches Lan Ha, which standard day cruises cannot
Both the famous bay and the quiet one in a single day
Vietnamese buffet lunch and welcome drink aboard
Hanoi transfer is optional: check your option covers it
Built for one day in the north rather than an overnight

fullDescription:
The Ha Long day trip with the drive fixed, which on this route is the part that decides how the day feels.

Hanoi to Ha Long is around two and a half hours each way on the expressway. That is five hours in a vehicle wrapped around six hours on the water, and the vehicle is what most people underestimate. A DCar limousine is a converted van with eight or nine reclining seats and real space between them, rather than sixteen upright seats on a tourist coach.

Pickup is in the Hanoi Old Quarter, which is where most visitors stay, so there is no getting yourself to a depot at dawn.

On the water you are among roughly 1,600 limestone islands, the tops of a karst range that kept going as sea levels rose. A day trip covers the central bay, which is the classic Ha Long and the busiest part of it.

An English-speaking guide is included throughout.

One thing to confirm when booking: the limousine transfer is listed as depending on the option selected, so check yours includes it rather than a shuttle bus. The price difference between the two options is almost entirely those five hours of road.

We book with Go Vietnam Trip Hanoi directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the VIP DCar limousine round-trip transfer according to your option, hotel pickup in the Hanoi Old Quarter and an English-speaking guide.

Six hours on the bay. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: DCar limousine: eight or nine reclining seats, not a coach
Five hours of the day are road, so the vehicle matters
Pickup in the Hanoi Old Quarter, no dawn trip to a depot
Roughly 1,600 karst islands in the central bay
Confirm your option includes the limousine, not a shuttle

fullDescription:
The Ha Long day trip with the meals and every activity already paid for.

This is the shuttle-bus version: the same bay, the same stops, the same six hours on the water, on a highway coach instead of a limousine. Everything that happens once you are on the boat is the full Ha Long day.

What matters more than the bus is what is included. Ha Long charges a bay entry fee plus separate tickets at the caves and at Ti Top Island, and a headline price without them can grow by a third at the jetties. Meals and all activities being covered means the day costs what it says.

The bay itself is roughly 1,600 limestone islands, the tops of a karst range that stayed above water as sea levels rose after the last ice age. A day trip covers the central bay, which is the classic view and the busiest water.

Bottled water is provided on the bus journey, and the shuttle uses the highway rather than the old road, which is what keeps the transfer to two and a half hours.

We book with Dragon King Viet Nam directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the round-trip highway shuttle if your option includes it, bottled water on the journey, meals and all activities.

Six hours on the bay. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Shuttle bus rather than limousine, and priced for it
Meals and all activities covered, not added at the jetty
Ha Long charges bay entry plus cave and island tickets
Roughly 1,600 karst islands, the classic central bay
Highway route keeps the transfer to two and a half hours

fullDescription:
Two days across Ninh Binh and Ha Long with every meal and transfer accounted for.

The pairing works because the two places are the same limestone in different settings. Ninh Binh's karst towers rise out of rice paddies with a river running between them, which is why it is called the inland bay; Ha Long's rise out of the sea. A day apart is enough to see them as one landscape.

The night is in a bungalow or hotel in Ninh Binh rather than on a cruise boat, which changes the trip's character and its price. A bungalow in Ninh Binh usually means being out among the karsts rather than in town, and you wake up in the landscape instead of on the water.

All meals are included, which on a two-day itinerary covering two provinces removes the running question of where and what to eat.

Transfers run by limousine or standard bus depending on the option chosen, so check which one yours is: the difference across two days and several hundred kilometres is considerable.

Water and wet wipes on the vehicle are a small thing that tells you the operator has done this route in July.

An English-speaking guide is with you throughout both days.

We book with Cozy Vietnam Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers full transfers by limousine or standard bus, an English-speaking guide, water and wet wipes on the vehicle, and all meals including one breakfast.

Two days, one night. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: The same karst inland in Ninh Binh and at sea in Ha Long
Night in a bungalow among the karsts, not on a boat
All meals included across both days
Check whether your option is limousine or standard bus
Guide with you throughout both days

fullDescription:
Five days that add Pu Luong to the usual northern circuit, which is what makes this trip worth the length.

Pu Luong is a nature reserve in Thanh Hoa province, four hours southwest of Hanoi, and it is a completely different landscape from the karst bays. Terraced rice fields climb the valley sides, Thai and Muong ethnic minority villages sit along the valley floor, and water wheels built from bamboo lift river water into the terraces. Two nights there is enough to walk between villages rather than drive past them.

The terraces have three good seasons and it is worth picking one. Around May and June they are flooded and mirror the sky. Through summer they are deep green. Just before the September and October harvest they turn gold, which is the month photographers aim for. Tell us which look you want and we will confirm the dates that hit it.

The rest of the route is the classic north: a night on a five-star cruise in Ha Long and Lan Ha, and a night in Ninh Binh where the same limestone rises out of rice paddies instead of the sea.

Four breakfasts are included along with the accommodation at each stop, running from a five-star cruise to four-star hotel and resort.

Five days is what it takes to include Pu Luong at all. Any shorter and the four-hour drive each way eats the value.

We book with Vacation Indochina Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers one night on a five-star cruise in Ha Long and Lan Ha, one night at a four-star hotel in Ninh Binh, two nights at a four-star resort in Pu Luong, and four breakfasts.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Pu Luong: rice terraces, Thai and Muong villages, bamboo water wheels
Two nights there, long enough to walk between villages
Three photogenic seasons: mirrored in June, gold before the October harvest
A night on a five-star cruise across Ha Long and Lan Ha
Five days is the minimum that makes Pu Luong worth the drive
